thread:
sam_support: Customer report — streaming request returned only two chunks, client saw socket EOF and retried. They were billed and our dashboard shows the request counted as 5xx. Customer is upset, asking for refund and root cause.

emma_eng: Can we get the request_id and timestamp? need the gateway logs and the edge proxy trace id.

sam_support: request_id: rq_2026-08-12_16:23:11_xYz, customer timestamp 2026-08-12T16:23:10Z. Attaching short curl they used to reproduce.

sam_support: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=redwood-13b"```

priya_infra: Got logs for rq_2026-08-12_16:23:11_xYz. Edge proxy (gateway-proxy v2.3.1) shows: upstream returned 200 OK and started chunked response, we wrote two chunks, then write to client failed with EPIPE. Our current classification path flags write failures after upstream started as a 5xx.

ben_carter: EPIPE = client closed socket while we were streaming. That should be a client abort, not a server 5xx. Looks like the billing classification conflates "upstream failure" with "client write failure."

alice_nguyen: Repro steps I tried from an unstable mobile link: simulate a client abort by killing the curl mid-stream: `curl ... | head -c 100 ; kill $PID`. Repro: gateway logs show write error and we currently emit status=502 in telemetry.

emma_eng: Thanks. Hypothesis: our gateway's metric emitter sets status_code=502 on any downstream write error after headers sent. Need to change to emit client_abort tag instead and avoid 5xx billing.

priya_infra: Quick log snippet (sanitized):
```
[edge-proxy] request_id=rq_2026-08-12_16:23:11_xYz upstream_status=200 bytes_sent=2048 error=write EPIPE
[billing] classify_request request_id=rq_2026-08-12_16:23:11_xYz label=5xx
```

ben_carter: Proposed fix: (1) update edge-proxy to distinguish write errors caused by client socket close (EPIPE/ECONNRESET) and set metric label client_disconnect, (2) change billing pipeline to only bill for 5xx if upstream returned >=500 or if gateway returned an explicit 5xx response code, not on write errors.

emma_eng: Also add a unit test: simulate chunked_transfer with client socket close and assert classification == client_abort and no billable 5xx.

priya_infra: I'll open infra ticket and schedule a canary. Plan: patch edge-proxy v2.3.2 with new classification flag, roll to canary region us-west-2 (10% traffic) for 48h, check client_disconnect metric and 5xx drop.

sam_support: Drafting response for customer: "thanks for the report — we found the traffic shows the client closed the connection mid-stream; our system incorrectly labeled the attempt as a 5xx and charged. We're rolling a fix and will refund the billed request. ETA for fix: 48-72 hours (canary -> prod)." Happy to post if folks agree. :thumbsup:

alice_nguyen: +1, include note about how to reproduce (kill curl) and that refunds will be processed for affected reqs.

ben_carter: Small edge case: if upstream actually returns a 5xx body and client closes, we should still treat as server error for metrics. So change must check upstream_status first, then downstream write error.

emma_eng: Good call. Implementation details: instrument request state machine with fields {upstream_status, wrote_headers, write_error_kind}. classify as 5xx only if upstream_status >= 500 or gateway generated a 5xx response. If wrote_headers==true and write_error_kind in (EPIPE, ECONNRESET) and upstream_status < 500 => client_abort.

deploy_bot: New PR created: github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/482 — tests + metric. CI: passed.

priya_infra: PR reviewed and merged to canary branch. Canaries scheduled.

sam_support: Customer notified about refund and tracking id ref-2026-08-12-R1. Will follow up after canary.

emma_eng: Follow-ups: add alert if client_abort spikes (to catch buggy clients/proxies) and add dashboard slice for "streaming client_disconnect vs genuine 5xx".

sam_support: Closing loop: thanks team. Will reopen if customer sees repeat behavior after patch. :pray:
